steps.title: Meet the fruit fly
steps.text: This 3D fruit fly is a model of a real insect's body. Drag it to spin it around. Scroll or pinch to zoom in.

steps.title: Pick any insect
steps.text: Tap another insect in this list to see its body. Beetles, bees, butterflies and flies all have Hox genes too.

steps.title: See the gene colours
steps.text: Tap Hox stain to colour each body segment by the Hox gene in charge of it. Hox genes are like bosses that tell each segment what to become.

steps.title: Switch genes on and off
steps.text: Each row is a gene. Each column is a body segment. Tap a square to switch that gene on or off there. A dot marks where the gene is normally on.

steps.title: Peek before you tap
steps.text: Point at a square, or tab to it, and this box tells you what would happen. Then tap to try it for real.

steps.title: A fly with four wings
steps.text: Here is the famous one: the Ubx gene is switched off in T3, the segment behind the wings. Watch the back of the fly: the tiny balancing knobs grow into a second pair of wings!

steps.title: What changed?
steps.text: This list tells you, in plain words, which body parts changed and what they turned into.

steps.title: Start over any time
steps.text: Press this to put the fly back to normal. Then make your own mutant, or press Surprise me for a random one.

steps.title: Learn as you go
steps.text: The Learn button opens short lessons. Each one has a quiz and a button that sets up the lab for you.

steps.title: Want the science details?
steps.text: Flip Scientist mode on to see where the facts come from: the real gene IDs, the research behind each change, and more experiments to try.
